import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insert_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def ins (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node v BinarySearchTree.Empty BinarySearchTree.Empty
  | BinarySearchTree.Node x l r =>
      if v < x then BinarySearchTree.Node x (ins l v) r
      else if v > x then BinarySearchTree.Node x l (ins r v)
      else BinarySearchTree.Node x l r
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def insert (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : insert_precond t v) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  ins t v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insert_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : insert_precond t v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∪ {v}
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma view_ins (v : Int) : ∀ t : BinarySearchTree, view (ins t v) = view t ∪ {v} := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | Empty => simp [ins, view]
  | Node x l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [ins]
    split_ifs with h1 h2
    · simp only [view, ihl]
      ext y
      simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      tauto
    · simp only [view, ihr]
      ext y
      simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      tauto
    · have hvx : v = x := by omega
      subst hvx
      ext y
      simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      tauto

lemma ins_bst (v : Int) : ∀ t : BinarySearchTree, is_bst t → is_bst (ins t v) := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | Empty =>
    intro _
    simp [ins, is_bst, view]
  | Node x l r ihl ihr =>
    intro h
    simp only [is_bst] at h
    obtain ⟨hl, hbl, hr, hbr⟩ := h
    simp only [ins]
    split_ifs with h1 h2
    · refine ⟨?_, ihl hbl, hr, hbr⟩
      intro y hy
      rw [view_ins] at hy
      rcases hy with hy | hy
      · exact hl y hy
      · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy
        omega
    · refine ⟨hl, hbl, ?_, ihr hbr⟩
      intro y hy
      rw [view_ins] at hy
      rcases hy with hy | hy
      · exact hr y hy
      · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy
        omega
    · exact ⟨hl, hbl, hr, hbr⟩
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem insert_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : insert_precond t v) :
    insert_postcond t v (insert t v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  refine ⟨ins_bst v t h_precond, ?_⟩
  exact view_ins v t
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## Analysis

The naive BST insert: on `Empty` create a leaf node; on `Node x l r`, if `v < x` recurse left, if `v > x` recurse right, otherwise (`v = x`) return the tree unchanged.

I define a helper `ins` (without preconditions) in the auxcode section so that induction is easy, then define `insert` as `ins`.

Two lemmas, both by structural induction on the tree:

1. **`view_ins`**: `view (ins t v) = view t ∪ {v}`. In the recursive branches we use the IH and pure set reasoning; in the equal branch we know `v = x`, so `v` is already in the view.
2. **`ins_bst`**: `is_bst t → is_bst (ins t v)`. The only nontrivial part is re-establishing the ordering condition on the modified subtree; by `view_ins` any element of `view (ins l v)` is either in `view l` (hence `< x`) or equals `v` (which is `< x` by the branch condition). Symmetrically for the right.

The postcondition then follows directly from the two lemmas.
